text: SMS: 'Your electricity will be disconnected tonight. Call 98xxx-xxxxx immediately to avoid a penalty.'
explanation: Threats of same-night disconnection plus a personal mobile number are classic scam signs. Check your bill on the provider's official app.

text: Bank app notification: 'Rs 1,500 was spent at a store with your card. Not you? Call the number printed on your card.'
explanation: This is a normal alert. It has no link, asks for no codes, and sends you to the number already on your card.

text: WhatsApp from an unknown number: 'We found your CV online. Pay Rs 2,500 registration to confirm your job.'
explanation: Real employers never charge you to hire you. Registration or training fees are the scam.

text: A buyer asks for your UPI PIN so they can 'send' you the money for your old phone.
explanation: A UPI PIN is only needed to SEND money. To receive money, share your UPI ID, never your PIN.

text: Email from your company's HR (a known address) about a team lunch on Friday. No links, no attachments.
explanation: Known sender, ordinary content, nothing to click and nothing sensitive requested.

text: Video caller in uniform: 'Your Aadhaar is linked to a crime. Stay on camera, tell nobody, and transfer money for verification.'
explanation: There is no 'digital arrest'. Real police do not demand money or secrecy on a video call.

text: SMS right after you place an order: 'Your OTP is 482910. Do not share it with anyone.'
explanation: It matches an action you just did. An OTP is only dangerous if you read it out to someone else.

text: Website pop-up: 'Your phone has 7 viruses! Call this number now for free removal.'
explanation: Websites cannot scan your phone like that. The 'technician' will ask you to install a remote-access app.

text: A message from your 'cousin's new number' asks for Rs 10,000 right now and says 'don't call, my voice is bad'.
explanation: Scammers avoid calls because you would notice the voice. Call the old number or ask family before sending anything.

text: Your regular delivery app: 'Your order is out for delivery. Share the delivery code only with the rider at your door.'
explanation: It comes from the app you used, matches an order you made, and the code is for the rider standing in front of you.

text: SMS: 'You won a free phone! Pay Rs 199 delivery charge to claim: free-phone-win.in'
explanation: You never entered a contest and a real prize does not ask for a fee. The payment page steals card details.

text: The official app store shows an update for the bank app you already have installed.
explanation: Updates through the official app store are safe. Be careful only with updates pushed through links in messages.

text: Telegram: 'Invest Rs 5,000 today and get Rs 25,000 in 7 days. Guaranteed returns!'
explanation: No genuine investment can guarantee returns, least of all 5x in a week.

text: You applied for a scholarship on the official portal. It emails a status update with no links and tells you to log in yourself.
explanation: You started it, there are no links, and it sends you to log in on your own. That is how genuine updates behave.

text: A caller wants you to install a remote-access app to 'fix' your internet connection.
explanation: Remote-access apps let them see your screen and approve payments. Never install one for a caller.
